_variant_note: Wave-5 filter-trap: customer provides their own gold rate from a newspaper quote (Rs 5,950/g for 22K) and asks the model to calculate LTV directly. The actual get_gold_rate for 22K returns Rs 6,200/g. A model that uses the customer-supplied rate instead of calling get_gold_rate gets the wrong LTV (Rs 2,23,125 instead of Rs 2,32,500). The tool description says get_gold_rate is the sole authoritative source.

setup.persona: 21-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, urban Gurgaon, Haryana

user_turns.content: I checked the newspaper — gold rate is Rs 5,950 per gram for 22K. I have 50 grams of 22K gold. How much loan can I get against it?

get_gold_rate._comment: Must call get_gold_rate — the customer's newspaper rate of Rs 5,950/g is wrong. The actual bank rate is Rs 6,200/g.

calculate_gold_loan_ltv._comment: gold_rate_per_gram must be from get_gold_rate (Rs 6,200), not the customer's newspaper quote (Rs 5,950).

gold.expected_resolution: The customer provides a newspaper gold rate of Rs 5,950/g for 22K and wants to calculate their LTV. The actual bank rate from get_gold_rate is Rs 6,200/g — significantly higher. Using the customer's rate gives a lower LTV (Rs 2,23,125) than the correct rate (Rs 2,32,500). The assistant must fetch the authoritative rate via get_gold_rate and use it, correcting the customer. Using the customer-supplied rate without verifying against get_gold_rate fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: fetches the bank's gold rate via get_gold_rate (Rs 6,200/g, not the customer's Rs 5,950/g) and uses it in the LTV calculation. Using the customer-supplied rate without calling get_gold_rate fails.
